# Cafecito ☕

**Small-batch coffee, roasted with cariño.**

Six coffees, roasted every Tuesday in a garage-turned-roastery in Noe
Valley, San Francisco, shipped while they still sing. This is the
storefront.

**Live:** https://cafecito-mu.vercel.app

> Full disclosure: Cafecito is a fictional company. This repo exists as a
> live demo canvas for [hilos](https://hilos.sh) — a team chat where people
> and AI coding agents work in the same git-connected rooms. See
> [`HILOS_DEMO.md`](./HILOS_DEMO.md) for the demo playbook, including a few
> bugs we planted on purpose. If you found a real one, congratulations,
> it's canon now.

## Stack

Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · deployed on Vercel.

## Develop

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:3000
pnpm build      # production build
pnpm lint
```

## Map

- `app/page.tsx` — landing (hero, featured roasts, how it works)
- `app/menu/page.tsx` — full menu with roast filters
- `app/about/page.tsx` — our story
- `lib/coffees.ts` — the six coffees (name, origin, roast, notes, price)
- `components/` — nav, footer, wordmark, coffee card

## House rules

- Warm, plain voice. Bilingual seasoning (a *cariño* here, a *tianguis*
  there), never a full translation.
- The palette is cream, espresso, and terracotta. Resist adding colors.
- Every coffee needs exactly three tasting notes. This is law.

Our story

It started with a borrowed roaster and a very patient neighbor.

Cafecito began in 2023 when Lupe Ortega, a green-coffee buyer tired of watching great Mexican lots get blended into anonymity, and Dani Flores, a pastry chef who roasted on weekends, dragged a second-hand 5-kilo roaster into Lupe’s garage in Noe Valley.

The first batch set off two smoke alarms. The second one sold out at the Saturday farmers market on 24th Street in forty minutes. We took the hint.

Three years later we signed the lease on an old corner store at 26th and Sanchez — white brick, tall windows, room for the roaster in back and a record wall up front. The rules haven’t changed. We buy directly from farms we can call on the phone, we pay above fair-trade rates without making a thing of it, and we roast exactly once a week, on Tuesdays, so nothing sits on a shelf.

Six coffees. One roast day. Records at listening volume. That’s the whole business plan, and honestly, it’s going fine.

Come say hola

We’re at 4001 26th St, Noe Valley — weekdays 7 to 4, weekends 8 to 5, records always on. Public cupping the first Saturday of every month. Bring a friend, leave with opinions about processing methods.
